sections.title: Overview and Bibliographic Identity

summary.text: Describes PCF as specifying how patient privacy consent directives are recorded, discovered, maintained and enforced over HL7 FHIR using the Consent resource and RESTful transactions, and tabulates its identity: canonical URL https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/PCF, version 1.1.0 (Trial Implementation, published 2023-08-04; NPM package ihe.iti.pcf@1.1.0 built 2024-02-23), FHIR 4.0.1, published by the IHE IT Infrastructure Technical Committee under CC-BY-4.0.

sections.extract: The IHE IT Infrastructure Technical Framework Supplement: Privacy Consent on FHIR (PCF) specifies how patient privacy consent directives are recorded, discovered, maintained, and enforced over HL7 FHIR resources using the FHIR Consent resource and RESTful transactions. sections.title: Volume 1 — Profiles: Privacy Consent on FHIR (PCF) (§1:53)

summary.text: Heading that opens Volume 1, the PCF profile (§1:53); it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: Actors and Transactions (§1:53.1)

summary.text: Names PCF's three actors with their CapabilityStatement canonicals: the Consent Recorder, which captures, updates and revokes a patient's consent directives and submits them to a Consent Registry; the Consent Registry, which stores, indexes, versions and serves Consent resources and their Provenance records; and the Consent Authorization Server, which evaluates active Consent directives from the Registry to return permit or deny on data access requests. All three interact through the Access Consent [ITI-108] transaction.

sections.extract: PCF defines three primary actors for privacy consent management and enforcement: Actor; Role in PCF; CapabilityStatement Canonical Consent Recorder; Captures, updates, and revokes patient privacy consent directives on behalf of a patient or authorized representative and submits them to a Consent Registry via [ITI-108] Access Consent.; https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/PCF/CapabilityStatement/IHE.PCF.consentRecorder

sections.title: Actor Options (§1:53.2)

summary.text: Lists the five [ITI-108] Access Consent options the Consent Recorder and Consent Registry support: Read (by logical id or version id), Search (by patient, status, date, period, actor, action, purpose, security-label, category or source-reference), Put (update, with a Provenance record), Post (create, with a Provenance record), and Delete (DELETE, or a status transition to inactive).

sections.title: Implicit Base Policy Sets (§1:53.2.1)

summary.text: Explains that a PCF Consent refines an underlying organisational or jurisdictional policy named in Consent.policy.uri, and that PCF arranges consent expressiveness into progressive profile levels; the text speaks of four levels but its table lists three. Basic Consent is a whole-record opt-in against a deny-by-default policy or opt-out against a permit-by-default one, optionally bounded by period and purpose; Intermediate Consent adds one level of nested exceptions scoped by purpose, actor, timeframe, data, or security label; Advanced Consent allows recursive trees of permit and deny sub-provisions over any combination of these.

sections.extract: A FHIR Consent resource under PCF refines an underlying organizational or jurisdictional privacy policy identified in Consent.policy.uri. summary.text: Heading that opens Volume 2, the Access Consent [ITI-108] transaction (§2:3.108); it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: Scope and Interaction Model

summary.text: States the scope of [ITI-108]: a Consent Recorder uses it to create, update, delete, read or search Consent resources on a Consent Registry, and a Consent Authorization Server, or a composite data-sharing actor such as a VHL Sharer, uses it to query a patient's active Consent directives before disclosing health information.

sections.extract: Transaction Access Consent [ITI-108] is used by a Consent Recorder to create, update, delete, read, or search Consent resources held on a Consent Registry, and by a Consent Authorization Server (or composite data-sharing actor such as a VHL Sharer) to query active Consent directives for a patient prior to disclosing health information.

sections.title: Message Semantics (§2:3.108.4)

summary.text: Specifies [ITI-108] as the FHIR RESTful API over HTTPS: create by POST (optionally in a transaction Bundle with an IHE.PCF.provenance resource recording who captured and attested the consent), update by PUT (e.g. revocation by setting status inactive, incrementing meta.versionId), logical delete of a Consent recorded in error, read and version read so an authorisation decision can cite the exact Consent.id and versionId, and search by patient, status, purpose, actor, period and date, security-label, and data references.

sections.extract: [ITI-108] uses the HL7 FHIR RESTful API over HTTPS: Create (POST [base]/Consent): Creates a new Consent resource conforming to IHE.PCF.consentBasic, IHE.PCF.consentIntermediate, or IHE.PCF.consentAdvanced. When submitted inside a FHIR transaction Bundle alongside a Provenance resource (IHE.PCF.provenance), records who captured the consent directive and how it was attested. sections.title: Required Elements on PCF Consent Profiles

summary.text: Lists the constraints the Basic, Intermediate and Advanced PCF profiles place on FHIR Consent: a required status (draft, active, inactive or entered-in-error; proposed and rejected prohibited in active enforcement), scope fixed to patient-privacy, a category including LOINC 59284-0, a required patient and at least one policy.uri, optional dateTime, performer, organization and source, and a provision carrying type (permit or deny), period, actor, action, HCS security labels, purpose of use from PCFPurposeOfUseVS (TREAT, ETREAT, HPAYMT, HOPERAT, HRESCH, PUBHLTH, PATRQT, FAMRQT, PWATRNY, SUPNWK), dataPeriod and data references.

sections.extract: Every PCF Consent instance (IHE.PCF.consentBasic, IHE.PCF.consentIntermediate, IHE.PCF.consentAdvanced) constrains the FHIR Consent resource as follows: Consent.status (1..1): draft | active | inactive | entered-in-error (proposed and rejected are prohibited in active enforcement). sections.title: Conformance Artefact Inventory in ihe.iti.pcf@1.1.0

summary.text: Inventories the conformance artefacts in the ihe.iti.pcf@1.1.0 package with their canonical URLs: the ImplementationGuide; CapabilityStatements for the Consent Recorder, Consent Registry and Consent Authorization Server; StructureDefinitions for the Basic, Intermediate and Advanced Consent profiles, the PCF Provenance profile and the StickToPatient extension; and the PCFPurposeOfUseVS value set plus five sensitivity value sets (substance use, behavioural health, paediatric behavioural health, opioid use disorder, psychiatry).
